questions.q: What are the four questions to ask before creating any field, per this lesson?
options: Color, icon, label, API name only
Type, constraint, who edits it, who sees it
Object, tab, app, profile
Price, discount, tax, currency
questions.explain: Type, constraints, field-level security (who edits), and page layout placement (who sees) are the four questions per field.

questions.q: Why is Status__c on Warranty_Claim__c built as a Picklist instead of free text?
options: Picklists load faster than text fields
Picklists are required on every custom object
Free text fields cannot be added to custom objects
A picklist only accepts predefined valid values, preventing typos and invalid statuses
questions.explain: A picklist restricts entry to a defined list (New/Review/Approved/Denied), which free text cannot enforce.

questions.q: What makes Total_Claimed__c, a Roll-Up Summary field, more reliable than a manually entered number field?
options: It's always correct automatically — no one has to remember to update it by hand
Roll-up summary fields are editable by any user
It requires no master-detail relationship to work
It stores more decimal places than a Number field
questions.explain: A roll-up summary recalculates automatically from its master-detail children, removing the risk of a stale manual entry.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is "just use text" called a worse default than it looks?
options: Text fields are more expensive in storage
Text fields cannot be placed on page layouts
Text fields enforce nothing — every typo becomes a real, reportable stored value
Text fields are deprecated in current Salesforce releases
questions.explain: Free text accepts anything, including typos and inconsistent values, unlike a picklist or formula field.

questions.q: What controls who is allowed to EDIT a specific field, as opposed to who can see it?
options: The object's API name
The app's branding settings
The Roll-Up Summary type
Field-level security, set by profile
questions.explain: Field-level security, configured per profile, controls edit (and view) access to a specific field — separate from page layout placement.
